annotationRationale: Monotonicity and signs locate and order the unique real roots. Inequality rules compare the odd powers, and induction supplies the Bernoulli bound used for choice E.
sourceMethod: Followed the official comparisons of increasing polynomials on (-1,0), including the Bernoulli bound for choice E. Justified root uniqueness by monotonicity and added a short proof of the bound.

review.mathCheck: Each polynomial is continuous and strictly increasing, with opposite signs at -1 and 0, so each has exactly one real root. On that interval, \(f_C>f_A>f_B\) and \(f_D>f_B\). The valid Bernoulli induction gives \(f_B(-2018/2019)<-2001<0\), placing B's root above E's as well. Choice B is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 21, page 12: the same polynomial comparisons and Bernoulli bound are used. Global odd-power monotonicity validly replaces Descartes' rule, and the added induction makes the bound reconstructable.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed root and monotonicity concepts fit. Inequality manipulation and induction appropriately support the argument; no calculus or definition-based difference proof is used.
